units.text: A plywood shack on a frozen lake, thick with the smell of wet wool and diesel.
Five holes have been drilled in the floor, and the black water in each one barely moves.
HALVARD EIDE, 60s, hunched on an upturned bucket, jigs a line and hums.
SUNNIVA ROE, 30s, sits opposite, a thermos between her boots.
BROCK DILLARD, 40s, leans against the door with arms crossed, steam rising off his shoulders, while INES CALLOWAY, 50s, rummages in a tackle box and TEAGUE, 20s, ties a lure with numb fingers.

Halvard pours coffee into the cap of the thermos and hands it to Sunniva, who passes it to Brock, who sips, grimaces, and passes it on to Ines, who takes it without looking up, and for a long minute nothing in the hut moves but the lines trembling in the holes.
Sixty years on this lake. Never a morning like it.
units.name: HALVARD

units.text: Brock shifts against the door and the latch, which has been hooked from the outside, does not lift.
